text:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] PROD latency p99 breach for chat.completions (route=chat.generate, region=us-east-1)
oncall-bot: details: model=mistral-8x, p99=1800ms, threshold=1500ms, window=1m, hosts=3
oncall-bot: paging: @sam (primary), @anya (secondary) :rotating_light:
sam: ack. seeing the alert in grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/chat?orgId=1&var-model=mistral-8x
sam: logs show a burst of long tail from a single tenant id=tenant-4315, spike started ~09:02 UTC
anya: on it. checking recent deploys and traffic shaping rules. no deploys in last 2 hours.
kevin: I see increased queue depth on the inference pool for mistral-8x, cpu on nodes 4/8 spiking, maybe batching caused tail.
sam: mitigation: enable fallback routing to cheaper-small model variant and scale up pool by +2 realtime instances (manual scale). lia, can you flip the fallback?
lia: flipping fallback now. runbook command: `./runbooks/fallback-route.sh --from=mistral-8x --to=mistral-8x-compat --duration=10m`
ops-runbook-bot: executed fallback-route for route=chat.generate, from=mistral-8x to mistral-8x-compat, expires in 10m
sam: fallback enabled, p99 dropped to 1100ms within 90s. paging noise reduced. :thumbsup:
anya: tenant-4315 is running a large A/B serving job — reached burst limit. I asked platform team to isolate and throttle.
kevin: root cause looks like workload burst + batching causing cache thrash for large sequence lengths. We'll need both infra and alert tuning follow-ups.
sam: quick customer impact note: we saw increased latency for ~3% of requests for 8 minutes, no errors returned, only higher latency. No SEV opened.
anya: recommend we adjust alerts to reduce noise: current p99 1500ms (1m window) fires for short bursts and pages SREs. Proposals:
- convert p99 alert to 5m rolling window for chat.generate to avoid paging on short bursts
- add per-model thresholds (mistral-8x has different perf profile vs small models)
- add an enrichment that ignores single-tenant bursts (if >60% of p99 from single tenant, suppress paging and open a ticket)
- keep p95 alert at lower threshold for faster detection of sustained regressions
kevin: +1. specific numbers we should try: p95 -> 350ms (was 300ms), p99 (5m) -> 2000ms for mistral-8x, p99 (5m) -> 1200ms for small models
lia: We should also create a dashboard that shows per-route, per-model p95/p99, and a tenant-breakdown panel. I'll stub a dashboard and share link.
sam: action items during post-incident:
- @kevin update alert rules in PrometheusAlertManager and add per-model labels (owner: kevin)
- @lia create dashboard and add tenant-breakdown panel (owner: lia)
- @anya open a follow-up with infra to investigate batching kernel selection for mistral-8x (owner: anya)
- @sam update runbook with new mitigation step for tenant-burst throttling and fallback routing (owner: sam)
ops-runbook-bot: note: remember to update `runbooks/alerts.md` with the new thresholds and the suppression heuristic.
sam: I'm going to lower noisy pages now: temporarily mute existing p99 alert until change lands. Will route future alerts to eng-sre only (no pager) during tuning window of 2 hours.
anya: agreed. please create a ticket: `ENGSRE-1241` with the proposed threshold table and attach a sample of tenant burst logs.
kevin: created ENGSRE-1241 and linked grafana panels + alert rules. PR for Prometheus `alerts/latency-chat.yaml` will be up in 30m.
lia: dashboard skeleton: https://grafana.redwood/d/latency/chat-per-model (preview) - added p95/p99 per model, tenant heatmap, and a small widget for 'burstiness' metric (p99_contrib_top_tenant).
sam: nice. once PR merges, we'll run for a day in monitor-only mode (no paging) and review false positives. If stable, promote to paging for p95 only and keep p99 as notify-only with pager suppression.
anya: for handoff: i'll be on call until 11:30 UTC then @kevin takes over. please DM for any immediate escalations.
sam: thanks all. will file a short incident blurb to #incidents later. Follow-up meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC to finalize thresholds and runbook edits.
kevin: quick note for postmortem: include cost impact of enabling fallback (~+3% token cost) and latency delta for end-users.
lia: adding runbook checklist: verify alert rules include `route` and `model` labels, test suppression logic in staging, and add runbook snippet for manual fallback command.
ops-runbook-bot: runbook updated: /runbooks/alerts.md (version bumped), /runbooks/fallback-route.sh (verified)
sam: closing thread. no more pages after fallback. will publish change-set once PR merges.
